subject: economics
chapter_title: Comparative Development Experiences of India and its Neighbours

concepts.title: Regional Economic Groupings
concepts.definition: Alliances formed by nations to integrate their economies, coordinate trade policies, and enhance global competitiveness.
concepts.key_idea: Nations form regional groups to expand their economic space and learn from neighbours' developmental strategies.
question_patterns: Why do nations form regional and global economic groupings?
Explain the importance of regional groupings in a globalised world.
What are the means used by countries to strengthen their domestic economies?
Name some regional economic groupings formed by developing and developed nations.
Explain regional economic groupings in your own words.

solution_steps.action: Identify the purpose of economic groupings
solution_steps.explain: Nations form groupings like SAARC, EU, ASEAN, G-20, and BRICS to strengthen domestic economies and face global competition collectively.

concepts.title: Comparative Development Timelines
concepts.definition: The historical timeline of planning and economic strategies initiated by India, China, and Pakistan since their inception.
concepts.key_idea: India and Pakistan started in 1947, China in 1949; all adopted planned development models.
question_patterns: When did India, China, and Pakistan start their development planning?
Compare the launch years of the first five-year plans of India, Pakistan, and China.
Which planning models did India and Pakistan adopt in their early stages?
What are the similarities in the developmental paths of India, Pakistan, and China?
Explain comparative development timelines in your own words.

solution_steps.explain: India and Pakistan became independent in 1947, while the People's Republic of China was established in 1949.
India's first five-year plan started in 1951, China's in 1953, and Pakistan's in 1956.

concepts.title: Great Leap Forward (GLF) Campaign
concepts.definition: A massive industrialisation campaign launched in China in 1958 to encourage backyard industries and collective farming through communes.
concepts.key_idea: Rapid industrialisation and agricultural collectivisation through the commune system.
question_patterns: Explain the Great Leap Forward campaign of China initiated in 1958.
What was the objective of the GLF campaign in China?
What problems did the Great Leap Forward campaign face?
How did the commune system work under the GLF campaign?
Explain great leap forward (glf) campaign in your own words.

solution_steps.explain: Initiated in 1958, it aimed to industrialise China on a large scale by encouraging people to set up backyard industries.
In rural areas, people collectively cultivated land under 26,000 communes covering almost the entire farm population.
A severe drought killed about 30 million people, and conflicts with Russia led to the withdrawal of Soviet professionals.

concepts.title: Great Proletarian Cultural Revolution
concepts.definition: An ideological and social campaign introduced by Mao Zedong in 1965 to send students and professionals to work and learn in rural areas.
concepts.key_idea: Sending urban youth and professionals to the countryside to bridge the gap between manual and intellectual work.
question_patterns: What was the Great Proletarian Cultural Revolution?
When was the Cultural Revolution introduced in China and by whom?
Describe the main feature of the Great Proletarian Cultural Revolution.
Why were students and professionals sent to the countryside in China?
Explain great proletarian cultural revolution in your own words.

solution_steps.explain: Mao Zedong introduced the revolution in 1965, running from 1966 to 1976.
Students and professionals were sent to live, work, and learn from the countryside.

concepts.title: Dual Pricing Policy
concepts.definition: A reform-era pricing mechanism where inputs and outputs are bought and sold at government-fixed prices for a set quota, and at market prices for any excess.
concepts.key_idea: Transitioning from a command economy to a market economy by using both state-determined and market-determined prices.
question_patterns: What is meant by dual pricing in the reform process of China?
How did the dual pricing system work for farmers and industrial units?
Explain the pricing mechanism adopted by China during its economic reforms.
Why did China introduce dual pricing instead of immediate complete price liberalisation?
Explain dual pricing policy in your own words.

solution_steps.explain: Dual pricing involves fixing prices in two ways: government-fixed prices and market-determined prices.
Fixed quantities of inputs and outputs were transacted at state prices, while the rest were traded at market prices.

concepts.title: Demographic Indicators
concepts.definition: Statistical metrics including population size, growth rate, density, sex ratio, fertility rate, and urbanisation used to compare population characteristics.
concepts.key_idea: China has the lowest density and growth rate (due to the one-child norm), while Pakistan has the highest growth and fertility rates.
question_patterns: Compare the demographic indicators of India, China, and Pakistan.
What was the impact of the one-child norm on China's demographic profile?
Why is the sex ratio low and biased against females in India, China, and Pakistan?
Which country among India, China, and Pakistan has the highest population density?
Explain demographic indicators in your own words.

solution_steps.explain: India and China have populations over 1.4 billion, while Pakistan is much smaller (240 million) but has the highest growth rate (1.96%).
China has the lowest density (150 per sq km) and highest urbanisation (65%), while India has the highest density (473 per sq km).
All three have low sex ratios due to son preference, and Pakistan has the highest fertility rate (3.4).

concepts.title: Sectoral Share of GVA and Employment
concepts.definition: The analysis of how agriculture, industry, and services contribute to a nation's total output (GVA) and how they employ the workforce.
concepts.key_idea: China followed the classical shift (agriculture to industry to services), while India and Pakistan shifted directly from agriculture to services.
question_patterns: Compare and contrast India and China's sectoral contribution towards GVA.
How does the distribution of workforce differ among India, China, and Pakistan?
Why is the service sector emerging as a major player of development in all three nations?
Which sector contributes the highest share to the GDP of India, China, and Pakistan?
Explain sectoral share of gva and employment in your own words.

solution_steps.explain: The service sector contributes the highest share in all three (54% in India/China, 55% in Pakistan).
Agriculture still employs the largest share in India (43%), while China has a higher share in industry (32%) compared to India and Pakistan (26%).

concepts.title: Human Development Indicators
concepts.definition: Socio-economic metrics such as life expectancy, schooling years, GNI per capita, infant and maternal mortality, and sanitation access used to assess well-being.
concepts.key_idea: China ranks significantly higher (78th) in HDI compared to India (130th) and Pakistan (168th).
question_patterns: Compare the human development indicators of India, China, and Pakistan.
Which country has the lowest infant mortality rate among India, China, and Pakistan?
How do India, China, and Pakistan compare in terms of maternal mortality rates?
What are the key indicators used to construct the Human Development Index?
Explain human development indicators in your own words.

solution_steps.explain: China has the highest HDI value (0.797, rank 78), followed by India (0.685, rank 130) and Pakistan (0.544, rank 168).
China has the lowest infant mortality (4.8) and maternal mortality (23), and has eliminated extreme poverty (0.0% national BPL).

concepts.title: Liberty Indicators
concepts.definition: Measures that evaluate the degree of civil liberties, democratic participation, rule of law, and independence of the judiciary in a society.
concepts.key_idea: HDI is incomplete without considering the extent of political freedom and constitutional protection of rights.
question_patterns: What are liberty indicators?
Give examples of liberty indicators.
Why is the construction of a human development index incomplete without liberty indicators?
How do liberty indicators supplement standard human development indicators?
Explain liberty indicators in your own words.

solution_steps.explain: They measure democratic participation, constitutional protection of rights, and judicial independence.
Standard HDI only measures economic and social indicators, neglecting political freedom and human rights.

concepts.title: Export-to-Import Ratio
concepts.definition: A quantitative measure of trade balance calculated as the percentage of exports relative to imports for a country with a specific trading partner.
concepts.key_idea: Evaluates trade surplus or deficit and bilateral trade dependency.
question_patterns: Calculate the export-to-import ratio of India with China.
Find the percentage of exports to imports for India's trade with Pakistan.
What is the ratio of exports to imports given exports of ... and imports of ...?
Compute the trade balance percentage using exports and imports.
Explain export-to-import ratio in your own words.

solution_steps.action: Divide exports by imports to find the basic ratio
solution_steps.explain: Divide the value of exports by the value of imports.

solution_steps.action: Multiply by 100 to get the percentage
solution_steps.explain: Convert the ratio into a percentage.

worked_examples.question: What is the ratio of exports to imports given exports of ... and imports of ...?
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Divide exports by imports to find the basic ratio. Step 2: Multiply by 100 to get the percentage. Working: exports / imports, ratio * 100.
worked_examples.answer: Export-to-Import Ratio applied step by step gives the required result.

worked_examples.answer: The method of export-to-import ratio leads to the required value or conclusion.
